To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
methylprednisolone inhibits the activation of AP- 1 and nuclear factor-κB (NF- κB) after spinal cord injury via a glucocorticosteroid receptor mechanism.

methylprednisolone suppresses the activation of activator protein- 1 and matrix metalloproteinases after spinal cord injury by inhibiting both activator protein- and nuclear factor-kappaB-dependent transcriptional cascades via a glucocorticosteroid receptor mechanism.
glucocorticoids inhibit post-traumatic inflammation by inhibiting the AP-1 transcription factor, which is activated in the injured spinal cords.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism of the beneficial effects of glucocorticoids in SCI.
the role of AP-1 and MMP expression in the pathophysiology of SCI and the mechanism of glucocorticoid-mediated suppression of post-traumatic inflammatory reactions after SCI.
the role of glucocorticoid receptors in the suppression of post-traumatic inflammatory gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucocorticoids suppress post-traumatic inflammation by inhibiting both AP-1 and the NF-κB pathways, and that AP-1 andNF-κB are involved in the expression of inflammatory genes such MMP-1 and -9.

The main takeaway from our work is that

glucocorticoids suppress post-traumatic inflammation through both AP-1 and nuclear factor κB pathways, and that the glucocorticoid mechanism of suppressing post-traumatic inflammation is mediated by the glucocorticoids binding to the glucocorticoidal receptor.
